name: Gnedenko: Fréchet domain of attraction
statement:
CumulativeDistributionFunction.isInMDAFrechet_iff (F : CumulativeDistributionFunction) {α : ℝ}
  (hα : 0 < α) :
  F.IsInMDAFrechet hα ↔
    ExtremeValueTheory.IsRegularlyVarying (fun x => 1 - ↑F.toStieltjesFunction x) (-α)
scope_note: Both directions. Eventual positivity inside regular variation encodes x_F = infinity. Explicit norming constants are not in the statement.

name: Gnedenko: Weibull domain of attraction
statement:
CumulativeDistributionFunction.isInMDAWeibull_iff (F : CumulativeDistributionFunction) {α : ℝ}
  (hα : 0 < α) :
  F.IsInMDAWeibull hα ↔
    ∃ xF,
      ↑F.toStieltjesFunction xF = 1 ∧
        (∀ x < xF, ↑F.toStieltjesFunction x < 1) ∧
          ExtremeValueTheory.IsRegularlyVarying (fun t => 1 - ↑F.toStieltjesFunction (xF - t⁻¹))
            (-α)
scope_note: Both directions, with x_F exactly the right endpoint. Explicit norming constants are not in the statement.

name: De Haan: Gumbel domain of attraction
statement:
CumulativeDistributionFunction.isInMDAGumbel_iff (F : CumulativeDistributionFunction) :
  F.IsInMDAGumbel ↔
    ((∀ (x : ℝ), ↑F.toStieltjesFunction x < 1) ∧
        ∃ f,
          (∀ᶠ (t : ℝ) in Filter.atTop, 0 < f t) ∧
            ∀ (x : ℝ),
              Filter.Tendsto
                (fun t =>
                  (1 - ↑F.toStieltjesFunction (t + x * f t)) / (1 - ↑F.toStieltjesFunction t))
                Filter.atTop (nhds (Real.exp (-x)))) ∨
      ∃ xF,
        (∀ x < xF, ↑F.toStieltjesFunction x < 1) ∧
          ↑F.toStieltjesFunction xF = 1 ∧
            ∃ f,
              (∀ᶠ (t : ℝ) in nhdsWithin xF (Set.Iio xF), 0 < f t) ∧
                ∀ (x : ℝ),
                  Filter.Tendsto
                    (fun t =>
                      (1 - ↑F.toStieltjesFunction (t + x * f t)) / (1 - ↑F.toStieltjesFunction t))
                    (nhdsWithin xF (Set.Iio xF)) (nhds (Real.exp (-x)))
scope_note: Both directions, x_F finite or infinite, one auxiliary function for all x. Stated as a disjunction of the two endpoint cases.

name: Von Mises condition for the Fréchet domain
statement:
CumulativeDistributionFunction.isInMDAFrechet_of_vonMises (F : CumulativeDistributionFunction)
  {α : ℝ} (hα : 0 < α) {z : ℝ} {F₁ : ℝ → ℝ}
  (h1 : ∀ x > z, HasDerivAt (↑F.toStieltjesFunction) (F₁ x) x)
  (hvm :
    Filter.Tendsto (fun x => x * F₁ x / (1 - ↑F.toStieltjesFunction x)) Filter.atTop (nhds α)) :
  F.IsInMDAFrechet hα
scope_note: A derivative of F near infinity instead of a density; positivity of the derivative is not assumed.

name: Von Mises condition for the Weibull domain
statement:
CumulativeDistributionFunction.isInMDAWeibull_of_vonMises (F : CumulativeDistributionFunction)
  {α : ℝ} (hα : 0 < α) {z xF : ℝ} (hz : z < xF) {F₁ : ℝ → ℝ}
  (h1 : ∀ x ∈ Set.Ioo z xF, HasDerivAt (↑F.toStieltjesFunction) (F₁ x) x)
  (hvm :
    Filter.Tendsto (fun x => (xF - x) * F₁ x / (1 - ↑F.toStieltjesFunction x))
      (nhdsWithin xF (Set.Iio xF)) (nhds α)) :
  F.IsInMDAWeibull hα
scope_note: A derivative of F near x_F instead of a density; F(x_F) = 1 is derived.

name: Von Mises condition for the Gumbel domain, infinite endpoint
statement:
CumulativeDistributionFunction.isInMDAGumbel_of_vonMises (F : CumulativeDistributionFunction)
  {z : ℝ} {F₁ F₂ : ℝ → ℝ} (h1 : ∀ x > z, HasDerivAt (↑F.toStieltjesFunction) (F₁ x) x)
  (h2 : ∀ x > z, HasDerivAt F₁ (F₂ x) x) (hpos : ∀ x > z, 0 < F₁ x)
  (hvm :
    Filter.Tendsto (fun t => (1 - ↑F.toStieltjesFunction t) * F₂ t / F₁ t ^ 2) Filter.atTop
      (nhds (-1))) :
  F.IsInMDAGumbel
scope_note: x_F = infinity only: the cited theorem also covers finite x_F, which is the separate entry von-mises-gumbel-finite. Together they give the book's result.

name: Von Mises condition for the Gumbel domain, finite endpoint
statement:
CumulativeDistributionFunction.isInMDAGumbel_of_vonMises_nhdsLT (F : CumulativeDistributionFunction)
  {z xF : ℝ} (hz : z < xF) {F₁ F₂ : ℝ → ℝ}
  (h1 : ∀ x ∈ Set.Ioo z xF, HasDerivAt (↑F.toStieltjesFunction) (F₁ x) x)
  (h2 : ∀ x ∈ Set.Ioo z xF, HasDerivAt F₁ (F₂ x) x) (hpos : ∀ x ∈ Set.Ioo z xF, 0 < F₁ x)
  (hF1 : Filter.Tendsto (↑F.toStieltjesFunction) (nhdsWithin xF (Set.Iio xF)) (nhds 1))
  (hvm :
    Filter.Tendsto (fun t => (1 - ↑F.toStieltjesFunction t) * F₂ t / F₁ t ^ 2)
      (nhdsWithin xF (Set.Iio xF)) (nhds (-1))) :
  F.IsInMDAGumbel
scope_note: x_F finite only, with F -> 1 at x_F as an explicit hypothesis (needed: atom-von-mises-counterexample). The infinite endpoint is the separate entry von-mises-gumbel-infinite.

name: The exponential law is in the Gumbel domain
statement:
CumulativeDistributionFunction.isInMDAGumbel_standardExponentialCDF :
  CumulativeDistributionFunction.standardExponentialCDF.IsInMDAGumbel
scope_note: An example; the standard exponential law only.

name: A finite-endpoint law in the Gumbel domain
statement:
CumulativeDistributionFunction.isInMDAGumbel_expNegInvCDF :
  CumulativeDistributionFunction.expNegInvCDF.IsInMDAGumbel
scope_note: An example: F(x) = 1 - exp(-x/(1-x)) on [0,1).

name: Quantile form of the domain of attraction condition
statement:
CumulativeDistributionFunction.isInMDAGEV_iff_exists_isExtendedRegularlyVarying_tailQuantile
  (F : CumulativeDistributionFunction) (γ : ℝ) :
  F.IsInMDAGEV γ ↔ ∃ a, ExtremeValueTheory.IsExtendedRegularlyVarying F.tailQuantile γ a
scope_note: Both directions, every extreme value index; the auxiliary function is existential.

name: IsInMDAGEV is convergence to gevCDF
statement:
CumulativeDistributionFunction.isInMDAGEV_iff_exists_tendsto_gevCDF
  {F : CumulativeDistributionFunction} (ξ : ℝ) :
  F.IsInMDAGEV ξ ↔
    ∃ As,
      ∀ (x : ℝ),
        Filter.Tendsto (fun n => ↑(As n • F).toStieltjesFunction x ^ n) Filter.atTop
          (nhds (↑(ExtremeValueTheory.gevCDF ξ).toStieltjesFunction x))
scope_note: For every xi and every x. The form at continuity points is isInMDAGEV_iff_exists_tendsto_gevCDF_of_continuousAt; gevCDF xi is continuous, so they agree.

name: The shape of a domain of attraction is unique
statement:
CumulativeDistributionFunction.IsInMDAGEV.unique {F : CumulativeDistributionFunction} {ξ η : ℝ}
  (hξ : F.IsInMDAGEV ξ) (hη : F.IsInMDAGEV η) : ξ = η
scope_note: Nothing left out.

name: Normal laws are in the Gumbel domain
statement:
CumulativeDistributionFunction.isInMDAGEV_ofMeasure_gaussianReal (m : ℝ) {v : NNReal} (hv : v ≠ 0) :
  (CumulativeDistributionFunction.ofMeasure (ProbabilityTheory.gaussianReal m v)).IsInMDAGEV 0
scope_note: Every mean and every positive variance. Membership only: the explicit constants are normal-norming-constants, for N(0,1).

name: Norming constants of the standard normal law
statement:
CumulativeDistributionFunction.tendsto_standardNormalCDF_pow (x : ℝ) :
  Filter.Tendsto
    (fun n =>
      ↑CumulativeDistributionFunction.standardNormalCDF.toStieltjesFunction
          (CumulativeDistributionFunction.normalScale n * x +
            CumulativeDistributionFunction.normalLocation n) ^
        n)
    Filter.atTop (nhds (↑standardGumbelCDF.toStieltjesFunction x))
scope_note: The textbook constants, for N(0,1), the law the book gives them for. The formulas are junk for small n, which does not matter in the limit.

name: Norming constants of the Gamma law
statement:
CumulativeDistributionFunction.tendsto_gammaCDF_pow {a r : ℝ} (ha : 0 < a) (hr : 0 < r) (x : ℝ) :
  Filter.Tendsto
    (fun n =>
      ↑(CumulativeDistributionFunction.gammaCDF a r).toStieltjesFunction
          (r⁻¹ * x +
            (Real.log ↑n + (a - 1) * Real.log (Real.log ↑n) - Real.log (Real.Gamma a)) / r) ^
        n)
    Filter.atTop (nhds (↑standardGumbelCDF.toStieltjesFunction x))
scope_note: Every real shape a > 0 and rate r > 0, not only Erlang. isInMDAGEV_gammaCDF is the membership statement.

name: Norming constants of the standard Cauchy law
statement:
CumulativeDistributionFunction.tendsto_standardCauchyCDF_pow (x : ℝ) :
  Filter.Tendsto
    (fun n =>
      ↑CumulativeDistributionFunction.standardCauchyCDF.toStieltjesFunction (↑n / Real.pi * x) ^ n)
    Filter.atTop (nhds (↑(standardFrechetCDF ⋯).toStieltjesFunction x))
scope_note: The standard law. Membership for every location and scale is cauchy-in-frechet-domain.

name: Cauchy laws are in the Fréchet domain
scope_note: Every location and every nonzero scale, index 1. No explicit constants for these.

name: IsInMDAGEV for iid sample maxima
statement:
CumulativeDistributionFunction.isInMDAGEV_iff_exists_tendsto_sampleMax.{u_1} {Ω : Type u_1}
  {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω} {P : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω} {F : CumulativeDistributionFunction}
  {X : ℕ → Ω → ℝ} (hF : ∀ (x : ℝ), ↑F.toStieltjesFunction x = P.real {ω | X 0 ω ≤ x})
  (hind : ProbabilityTheory.iIndepFun X P)
  (hid : ∀ (t : ℕ), ProbabilityTheory.IdentDistrib (X t) (X 0) P P) (ξ : ℝ) :
  F.IsInMDAGEV ξ ↔
    ∃ a b,
      (∀ (n : ℕ), 0 < a n) ∧
        ∀ (x : ℝ),
          Filter.Tendsto
            (fun n => P.real {ω | (ExtremeValueTheory.blockMax X n 0 ω - b n) / a n ≤ x})
            Filter.atTop (nhds (↑(ExtremeValueTheory.gevCDF ξ).toStieltjesFunction x))
scope_note: The law of the sample maximum, normalized by a_n > 0 for all n. Iid random variables with c.d.f. F.

name: Canonical norming constants
statement:
CumulativeDistributionFunction.exists_tendsto_pow_norming_tailQuantile
  {F : CumulativeDistributionFunction} {γ : ℝ} (hF : F.IsInMDAGEV γ) :
  ∃ a,
    ExtremeValueTheory.IsExtendedRegularlyVarying F.tailQuantile γ a ∧
      ∀ (x : ℝ),
        Filter.Tendsto (fun n => ↑F.toStieltjesFunction (a ↑n * x + F.tailQuantile ↑n) ^ n)
          Filter.atTop (nhds (↑(ExtremeValueTheory.gevCDF γ).toStieltjesFunction x))
scope_note: Every shape: F(a(n) x + U(n))^n -> gevCDF(x), for every x, with a the auxiliary function of the tail quantile function U.

name: The unified von Mises condition, infinite endpoint
statement:
CumulativeDistributionFunction.isInMDAGEV_of_vonMises (F : CumulativeDistributionFunction) {z γ : ℝ}
  (hγ : 0 ≤ γ) {F₁ F₂ : ℝ → ℝ} (h1 : ∀ x > z, HasDerivAt (↑F.toStieltjesFunction) (F₁ x) x)
  (h2 : ∀ x > z, HasDerivAt F₁ (F₂ x) x) (hpos : ∀ x > z, 0 < F₁ x)
  (hvm :
    Filter.Tendsto (fun t => (1 - ↑F.toStieltjesFunction t) * F₂ t / F₁ t ^ 2) Filter.atTop
      (nhds (-γ - 1))) :
  F.IsInMDAGEV γ
scope_note: gamma >= 0 and x_F = infinity only, with the sign as a hypothesis (gamma < 0 should be impossible here, which is not mechanized): the cited theorem also covers finite x_F, which is the separate entry von-mises-unified-finite.

name: The unified von Mises condition, finite endpoint
statement:
CumulativeDistributionFunction.isInMDAGEV_of_vonMises_nhdsLT (F : CumulativeDistributionFunction)
  {z xF γ : ℝ} (hz : z < xF) (hγ : γ ≤ 0) {F₁ F₂ : ℝ → ℝ}
  (h1 : ∀ x ∈ Set.Ioo z xF, HasDerivAt (↑F.toStieltjesFunction) (F₁ x) x)
  (h2 : ∀ x ∈ Set.Ioo z xF, HasDerivAt F₁ (F₂ x) x) (hpos : ∀ x ∈ Set.Ioo z xF, 0 < F₁ x)
  (hF1 : Filter.Tendsto (↑F.toStieltjesFunction) (nhdsWithin xF (Set.Iio xF)) (nhds 1))
  (hvm :
    Filter.Tendsto (fun t => (1 - ↑F.toStieltjesFunction t) * F₂ t / F₁ t ^ 2)
      (nhdsWithin xF (Set.Iio xF)) (nhds (-γ - 1))) :
  F.IsInMDAGEV γ
scope_note: gamma <= 0 and x_F finite only, with F -> 1 at x_F and the sign as hypotheses (gamma > 0 should be impossible here, which is not mechanized). The infinite endpoint is von-mises-unified-infinite.
